description: A *factoring* splits the variables of a planning task into a *center* and *leaves* for decoupled search. The inverted fork factoring uses the *causal graph*, which has an arc from variable `u` to `v` when some operator reads or writes `u` and writes `v`. Every *source component* of this graph (a strongly connected component that no arc enters) becomes a leaf, if it has at most 2^16 states; all other variables form the center. The center may read the leaves, but the leaves never read the center. It suits tasks where independent parts supply preconditions to a shared component.
